support_quote: Participants were recruited from four U.S. institutions between June 2019 and February 2022. Inclusion criteria required participants to be 18 years or older, have available VA data, and be able to communicate in English to complete the 100-item visual acuity survey. All participants were naïve to the items at enrollment. The recruitment aimed to include individuals across a broad spectrum of visual function
notes: q1: sampling method not described here (deferred to ref 7). q2: purposive sampling 'across a broad spectrum' with 68.6% below 0.3 logMAR is spectrum-enriched; not a classic two-gate design, so U not N. Applicability High: authors say the sample has 'fewer normally sighted individuals than the general population' (page 8), so prevalence and PPV/NPV do not transfer to a screening population.

support_quote: The 20 items with the highest AUC at each threshold were retained as primary candidates for subsequent pairing. ... Each of the top 20 items was paired with each of the remaining 99 (yielding 1980 unique combinations per threshold).
notes: q1: self-report; not stated whether the survey preceded VA measurement or whether participants knew their VA/diagnosis. q2: the response rule ('no' = positive) is fixed, but the item (1 of 100) and item pairs (1 of 1980) were chosen by maximising AUC in the same sample, so the reported accuracy is optimistic. q3: no split-sample or external validation ('It is possible that the performance of individual items or short combinations might differ if administered independently, outside the context of the longer survey.', page 8). Applicability High: items were answered inside a 100-item survey, not as stand-alone screening questions; a reviewer treating wording alone as the test may lower this to Unclear.

support_quote: VA with habitual correction was assessed using standardized charts (Bailey–Lovie, ETDRS, or Snellen). When both monocular and binocular measurements were available, we used binocular VA; when only monocular measurements were available, VA from the better seeing eye was used.
notes: q1: standard charts, habitual correction; mixed chart types across sites. q2: blinding of VA examiners to survey answers not stated. q3: thresholds VA <= 0.3 and <= 1.0 logMAR are fixed clinical definitions stated in the abstract (page 1). q4: VA protocol deferred to the earlier publication. Applicability Low for a VA-defined target condition; note the authors' caveat that field-only loss is missed (page 8).

support_quote: This analysis included 385 participants from a cohort described previously.
notes: q1: interval between survey and VA measurement not reported. q2: 'available VA data' was an inclusion criterion, so all analysed participants had a reference standard. q3 answered N because some had binocular VA and others better-eye monocular VA, on different charts; judged a minor deviation (same construct, differences of ~0.1 logMAR) so the domain is kept at Unclear rather than High. q4: Table 1 N = 385 matches the analysed n; 2x2 counts are not tabulated, so sensitivity/specificity must be back-calculated for extraction.

support_quote: Among subjects in the Montreal area not eligible for other components of the CSHA, all positive subjects, along with a random sample of negative subjects, were selected to undergo a visual examination at home.
notes: q1: frame was a random population sample aged >= 65 ('A random sample of individuals aged at least 65 years was drawn for each selected area', page 2). q2: not sampled on disease status. q3: exclusions were logistic (eligibility for other CSHA components), not vision-related. q4 N: the validation subsample was selected on the index test (all positives, random negatives) and 'the sensitivity and specificity estimated in this study cannot be applied to an unselected population' (page 2); crude estimates reported. Applicability Low: community-dwelling older adults, the setting where such a screen would be used.

support_quote: Data on visual impairment were collected during a home interview carried out as part of the CSHA study. ... a visual disability was considered to be present if the answer to at least one of the following two questions was positive
notes: q1: questionnaire answered at the home interview, about 6 months before the eye examination, so answers could not be influenced by the measurement. q2: the two yes/no items and the four test criteria (near item; distance item; >= 1 positive; 2 positive) were specified in Methods (page 3). q3: items taken unchanged from Statistics Canada HALS surveys, not selected on this sample. q4: same interviewer-administered mode for all. Applicability Low: two brief self-report questions, exactly the review's index test.

support_quote: The first author (JG), an optometrist who was not aware of the subjects’ questionnaire responses at the time of the examination, carried out the visual assessment.
notes: q1: 'Distance VA was measured at 4 m using the Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Survey charts17 in a back-lighted box.18 Near VA was measured at 0.4 m' (page 2; 17 and 18 are flattened reference superscripts); presenting and best-corrected VA. q2: examiner blinded (quoted). q3: ICD-9 categories and four diagnostic criteria (VA <= 6/12; VA <= 6/21) prespecified (pages 2-3). q4: measured for the study with a stated protocol. Applicability Low: VA <= 6/21 is the rehabilitation-centre eligibility threshold in Quebec (page 4), so the target condition is close to LVR need.

support_quote: Among the 144 subjects eligible for the second stage of the study, 31 were lost to follow-up and 42 refused to participate. We were unable to schedule an eye examination before the end of the study for six of the remaining 71 subjects. Among the 65 subjects who received the visual examination, 19 had at least one positive response to the questionnaire, and 46 had two negative responses. The final participation rate was 45.1%
notes: q1 N: about 6 months between questionnaire and examination ('the long interval (approximately 6 months) before recontacting the subjects', page 6) in people aged >= 65. q2 N: partial verification; only 65 of 144 eligible (45.1%) examined, and eligibility itself depended on the index test. q3: same examination for everyone verified. q4: all 65 examined appear in Table 4, but cell counts are not given and CIs are very wide ('Due to the small number of true positives, the precision of the crude sensitivity and of the PPV was very low', page 4). Do not pool crude sensitivity/specificity from this design without reweighting.
